Hi Karthik,

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary here, I attached a compact processing matrix (processing_matrix_2027-03.pdf) and listed the high-level commitments below; Marissa (CS lead) looped in for runbook/ops details.

- Compute vs control plane: inference execution (model forward pass and KV cache) runs in the compute region you select (we support us-west, us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast). Control plane metadata (routing, billing, model metadata) is processed in a separate control plane region (us-central) but is encrypted and access-controlled; we provide per-tenant separation on Dedicated/Private.

- Subprocessors: primary compute and storage are with our cloud provider partners (region-specific). For telemetry and logs we use LogStream Inc. (logs scrubbed of PII by default) and MetricsCo for aggregated traces. The attached matrix enumerates per-region subprocessors and the exact data elements they may see.

- Deletion SLA: user-requested deletion for active tokens/objects: 24–72 hours for immediate deletion from primary stores (typical case ~24h). Backups: 60–90 days depending on backup cadence; we provide an option for expedited purge for enterprise contracts (30 days SLA) and a documented cert of deletion once completed.

- Cross-border transfers: when you select a compute region we confine execution to that region; any fallbacks (capacity, failover) are governed by policy and will not cross regions unless you authorize cross-border execution or use our hosted default routing. We document transfer hops and subprocessors in the attached matrix.

If you want, Neha (security) can assemble the SOC2 excerpt and the subprocessor inventory snapshot for procurement. Next steps: tell me the regions you expect to use and whether you require a contract-level commitment on deletion SLA (we can include expedited purge in the SOW).

Best,

Hi Olivia — quick operational clarifications to supplement Karthik's note:

- Isolation: For Dedicated and Private customers we offer tenant isolation at the compute level (pinned GPU pools) so no noisy neighbor cross-tenant execution. For Hosted customers we use strict tenant namespaces and quotas; compute still executes in the chosen region but may share instance classes.

- Telemetry: We scrub user-level prompt/response content from platform metrics by default. Retained telemetry is hashed and aggregated; raw prompt/response is treated as customer content and retained only per your retention policy. We can offer a telemetry opt-out in the contract.

- Subprocessor handling: the inventory lists subprocessors and their roles (compute, monitoring, backups, key management). Each subprocessor has a contract with SOC2+ or equivalent controls; if you need vendor attestations we can provide them under NDA.

Two asks from our side to help scope the SOW: 1) which regions would you like pinned for execution; 2) do you require an expedited deletion SLA (30 days) in the contract?

Thanks,

Hi Olivia / team — attaching the current inventory and summary you requested.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_2027-02.csv, soc2_summary_2026.pdf

Key points from the evidence pack:
- Subprocessor inventory includes region tags and the minimal data categories each partner may access (compute, ephemeral cache, billing metadata, aggregated telemetry).
- SOC2 summary includes scope (platform availability + security) and the last assessment date (2026-11). Full reports are available under NDA.
- Deletion: standard workflow
  * Active data: removal from primary stores once a deletion request is processed — typical completion 24 hours; cert issued after internal validation.
  * Backups & snapshots: removed per backup retention windows; standard retention 60–90 days. For Nimbus Health we can include an expedited purge term in the SOW with an obligation to complete backup purges within 30 days after issuance of purge request.

Process note: to issue the deletion cert we require an authorized contact and a request ticket (we can accept procurement or security manager approvals). Once the ticket is closed we'll supply a signed attestation (doc link provided below).
